13. On dissection of materials placed on record, after marshaling of facts in issue and after hearing erudite counsel appearing for combating parties, this Tribunal opines that this issue is pregmented with inner issues such as :

It is the specific contention of the petitioner that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the RTA on 19.12.2018 at 8.00 a.m..

15. It is a settled principles of law that the negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
16. Reverting back to the factual matrix the petitioner in order to prove the negligence of respondent has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 to 7 being police documents.
The criminal law was set into motion in Ex.P.2 FIS on 19.12.2018.
On the basis of Ex.P.2 FIS, even the FIR was lodged on the same day.
The main documents which sheds light on the factum of negligence is Ex.P.3 and 4 being spot mahazar and Spot Sketch.
On careful perusal of Ex.P3 and 4 it reflects that the petitioner himself had dashed the Tempo Traveller to its hind side.
Further on close perusal of the Ex.P3 Spot Mahazar it reflects that the total width of the road is 40 feet.
The accident had occurred at the left side of the road.
The exact place of impact and the road margin was not mentioned either in Ex.P3 and Ex.P4.
When such being the case it is relevant to dwell into the cross examination of PW.1.
PW.1 has categorically admitted that, he was going very close to the Tempo Traveler on the date of accident.
It is relevant to note that, one has to maintain certain safe distance between the vehicle.
The petitioner has also videly contributed for the accident.
Further PW.1 has also admitted that the Tempo Traveller has stopped half in the footpath and other half on the road.
He further denied the contents of Ex.P4.
PW.1 has also admitted that the chargesheet was filed as against him and he pleaded guilty before the criminal court.
Only for the reason that he has pleaded guilty before the criminal court that does not means that there is no negligence on the part of the Tempo Traveller driver.
Abruptly stopping the vehicle on the road shows that there is negligence on the part of the Tempo Traveller driver also.
17. Further if petitioner was coming in a normal speed then he would have certainly avoided the accident.
Having regard to the place of accident and topography of the accident happened it could be easily culled out that the petitioner has also contributed negligence equally.
It could be culled out from the petition averments itself that the petitioner himself had dashed the Tempo Traveler from the hind side.
18. It is the the case of the petitioner that, the Tempo Traveler driver had abruptly stopped the Tempo Traveler without giving any indications as such the accident happened.
No doubt the rider of the motorcycle i.e., the petitioner herein had a clear line of vision and could not have missed seeing the Tempo Traveler which was going ahead on the road.

But the very act of the driver of the Tempo Traveler in stopping the said vehicle on a road abruptly that too without putting on the indicators itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver
What also deserves notice is that the petitioner has not maintained the safe distance as he himself has admitted during the course of cross examination.

Under such circumstances, it appears in all probability that by the time the petitioner realized the fact that the Tempo Traveler immobile, it would have been too late for him to react and check or divert his vehicle to avoid collision.

It is needless to say that the injuries No.1 to 3 and 5 are simple and injury No.4 is grievous in nature.
The discharge summary issued by Aster CMI Hospital, indicate that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 19.12.2018 to 22.12.2018 (4 days in total).

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
It is the case of the petitioner that the accidental injuries have caused him permanent disability.
However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.

21. Further during the course of his cross-examination the petitioner himself admitted that now he is working in MK Food catering services and now he is getting more than Rs.25,000/- salary per month.
In view of the decision reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439, 'If the claimant has continued in service, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.'
That is to say as the actual financial loss arising out of physical disability is not made out by the claimant, he is not entitled for compensation towards 'loss of future income'.
22. Though PW.1 deposed in his evidence affidavit that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to attend his work, he has not produced any leave letter addressed to his employer.
So also no iota of evidence is placed on record to show that he has not received salary during treatment period.
Non-production of the any documents in this regard results in drawing of an inference that he has not suffered any financial loss during the period of his treatment.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.

ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 4 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take him care by leaving their duties.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day and a sum of Rs.6,000/- (1,500 X 4) is awarded under this head.
24. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P10, the petitioner has spent Rs.1,38,649/-
towards medical expenses.
On perusal of Sl.No.11 of Ex.P.10 for a sum of Rs.700/-, in the amount column it is mentioned as 'zero only'.
Hence the said amount is excluded from the total bills amount.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross- examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for (Rs.1,38,649 - Rs.700) Rs.1,37,949/-
which is rounded off to Rs.1,38,000/- towards medical expenses.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
27. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

32. ISSUE NO.3

: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed U/Sec. 166 of M.V Act is hereby allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,12,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. interest is waived off from the date of filing of petition till the commencement of evidence (i.e, from 07.03.2019 to 31.03.2023).
Further he is entitled interest from the date of evidence till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire award amount together with interest, shall be released to the petitioner by way of E-payment on proper identification and confirmation.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
